links.note: BSP formed 1984 under Kanshi Ram is the recognised-national-party roster entry. Recall of a named party's founding still sits on the concept that roster is, 24099, rather than on any generic concept.

BSP's stated inspirations (Sahu Maharaj, Phule, Ramaswami Naicker, Ambedkar) are listed in the same national-party entry. 24091 Partisanship and ideology states the general principle; this is recall of one national party's entry.
The 6-per-cent-in-four-states plus four-Lok-Sabha-seats test is 24099's description exactly. 24100 State parties carries the other, lower threshold, which this stem does not ask for.

BJP's guiding philosophy is an attribute of its national-party entry (which names both cultural nationalism/Hindutva and integral humanism). Same concept as qid:87519 in part 1, which keys the other of those two phrases.
Founder of BSP, straight recall from the national-parties roster.
China as the country with a single party allowed to control government is 24096's description. The sibling 24097 two-party and 24098 multi-party are excluded by the stem naming 'single-party'.

Tests the boundary of the definition: BJP, INC and BSP contest elections and hold power, the odd one out does not. That boundary is 24090 (a group that contests elections and holds power), not 24099, which is about the recognition threshold rather than about what makes a body a party at all.

NCP is a recognised national party whose roster entry names Maharashtra as its major base with presence in Meghalaya, Manipur and Assam - the three distractors are lifted from that same sentence. So it is 24099, not 24100 State parties, despite the stem asking about a state.

Key is that no country chooses its party system; it evolves with the society's social and regional divisions. Of the three system concepts, only 24098 carries that societal-fit clause ('suited to a large and diverse society'), and India's multi-party system is the text's worked case for why systems differ. 24096 and 24097 describe particular systems, not why a country has one.

'Centrist' is the ideological label in the Congress national-party entry. Sibling 24091 Partisanship and ideology holds the general principle that parties have an ideology; this item is recall of one recognised national party's stated orientation.
BJP founded 1980 - date recall from the national-parties roster; the concept the date sits inside, not a timeline.
USA and UK together are 24097's named examples of power alternating between two major parties.
NDA, UPA and Left Front in 2004 are the text's illustration that several parties compete and alliances form governments - 24098. Not 24099, which is about which parties count as national.
China as the one-party state, against India/USA/UK. 24096 by its description; the distractors are the two-party and multi-party cases.

The term 'recognised' and the unique election symbol come from the registration-and-recognition paragraph that defines recognised parties, whose criterion 24099 states. 24103 also mentions the Election Commission but only as a reform agency, which this is not about.

Socialism, secularism, democracy, opposition to imperialism and communalism, socio-economic justice - all three statements are the CPI(M) national-party entry verbatim, so the item is recall of that entry.

The statement that fails is 'parties reflect fundamental political unity in a society' - the text says divisions, and a party takes a partisan stand. That is 24091. The other two statements (persuading voters, winning support through elections) belong to 24093, but they are the true ones and not what the item turns on. NOTE: the printed key 'All the above' is wrong - only statement A is incorrect.

Registration with the Election Commission, equal treatment, and special facilities for large and established parties is the paragraph that introduces recognised parties, which 24099 covers. Distinct from 24103, where Election Commission regulation appears as a proposed reform.
